subject: Re: Encord/Neosapience - Next Steps ahead of Monday's Demo
text:
Hi Alex,

Thank you for the follow-up.

Concerning the Managed Service Annotators, we can confirm the list of languages and their approximate data volumes for audio annotation. Each language has approximately 200 hours of data:

Arabic, Cantonese, Chinese, English, French, German, Hindi, Indonesian, Italian, Japanese, Korean, Malay, Polish, Portuguese, Russian, Spanish, Spanish-Latin, Taiwan, Thai, Vietnamese

For video data, we anticipate processing around 200 hours of data. The video data itself isn't language-specific in the same way as the audio, so we don't have a breakdown by language for this.

To help us better understand the potential costs involved, could you please provide an estimate of the cost for annotating this volume of audio and video data? We'd also like to clarify that the annotation we require is in the form of MOS (mean opinion score) testing.

Regarding the demonstration, we would like to postpone the demonstration scheduled for Monday. We would like to first receive the cost estimate and then, based on that information, decide whether to proceed with the demonstration and your services.

Please let us know if you require any further information.

Best regards,

Younggun Lee

subject: RE: Redlines for Encord MSA
text:
Alastair, Nick,

Thanks for bearing with me. Here are the points that ought to keep us busy for our call.

 *   5.1.1 and 5.1.2 – these restrict Invisible’s ability to make use the platform as intended. This point should be led by the business, more so than legal. Invisible retains agents to run tasks for the benefit of its own clients. These paragraphs run counter to the core use case for Encord’s platform.
 *   5.1.10 – Invisible doesn’t agree to this kind of far-reaching commitment. We agree with 5.1.9 and other contract-led restrictions. But a wide claim on “acting contrary to Encord IP” is future-facing and ambiguous.
 *   7.7 – Security Standard – It’d be great to complete this section with commitment to ISO-27001 or a SOC-II Type 2 to further illustrate how 7.7 is interpreted.
 *   8 – IP – Encord struck the IP clause to INV’s benefit. You’ll understand that we require confirmation of ownership of Deliverables (as defined).
 *   10.6 – Invisible does not provide indemnification to its vendors. So long as we agree to read 10.6 as not including an obligation to defend, it can remain. Let’s make sure we align on what’s expected.
 *   Liability – more balance is required (i.e. 11.1 should be mutual). Further, we cannot agree to any uncapped obligations, nor indirect damages. We’d prefer to negotiate a mutual supercap for certain claims, and agree to have Encord be bound by those for some core risks as well (i.e. as a trade-off for removing uncapped liability, we’d agree to have data breaches by Encord capped at the supercap).

Looking forward to meeting and discussing this later today,

Paul

text:
Hi Alex,

Thank you for the detailed information and your understanding of our needs. We appreciate you taking the time to explain your process and the value of experienced annotators for MOS testing. We understand that preparing a quote, especially for less common languages, requires effort on your end, and we appreciate that.

As we discussed in our previous communication, our primary focus at this stage is on sourcing annotators with diverse language backgrounds. We also want to be transparent that we don't currently have a concrete plan for how we will be utilizing RL. This makes it difficult for us to provide specific details about budget, processing time, and the relative importance of each language, as our needs are still somewhat fluid. We are still in the early stages of exploring how RL can fit into our workflow, and our plans for this are not yet fully formed. Therefore, we are concerned that any discussion about RL at this point may be premature and lead to miscommunication. We anticipate having a clearer picture of our RL strategy and annotation requirements within the next few months. At that point, we would be very interested in revisiting the possibility of working with Encord.

Regarding Monday's demonstration, we would like to cancel and reconnect at a later date when we have a more defined strategy.

Thank you again for your patience and understanding. We appreciate your efforts in trying to accommodate our needs. We look forward to connecting with you again in the future.

Best regards,

Younggun

Hi Anurag,

I am exploring with adding metadata to our uploaded aws images and I had some questions about how to add metadata per image. It appears that we can add "imageMetadata" per image but are limited to mimeType, fileSize, width, and height, and then we can add "clientMetadata" with custom metadata fields but it looks like that would apply to the whole image folder I would be uploading. Our use case is the following:

We are uploading aws folders with the file structure "s3://{bucket_name}/{date_collected}/{robot_state}/{image_name}".
